text:
ben (acme-admin): Hey support — after rotating a service API key the project dashboard actions are greyed out and every click returns 403. Happened ~10m after rotation. Org: acme-inc, project: payments-prod. Can share logs if helpful.

alice (support): Sorry you're seeing that, Ben. Quick Qs: which key did you rotate (service token vs personal key)? Can you paste the exact curl you ran that gets the 403 and a request-id from the browser console/network tab?

ben (acme-admin): It was a service API key generated under Project Settings -> Service keys. Here is a minimal repro from our side:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_service_8x9x" https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/projects/pm-123/actions 
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{ "error": "forbidden", "message": "insufficient_project_permission" }
```
Request-id from console: rq_20240302_9881f3. I haven't tried logout yet. UI still shows me as project admin in the members list.

alice (support): Thanks — that helps. This looks specific to service-key rotation causing an authz mapping to lag (service tokens aliasing). I'm going to escalate to engineering and try a couple quick workarounds: 1) Can you try a personal API key to confirm it's scoped correctly? 2) If you can, try logging out of console and back in to refresh claims. I'll loop in eng.

deploy-bot: [system] Started background job authz-resync for org acme-inc (job id: 98765).

ben (acme-admin): Tried logging out/in — no change. Personal key (user token) works for the same API call and returns 200. So it's limited to the service key.

dmitri (eng): +1 — pinged from support. I can see the request-id in logs. The service token alias table didn't update the binding for the new key alias; console action checks against token_alias -> principal mapping and gets a stale entry, so checks fail. TTL should have forced a refresh but there was a race with the token rotation path.

carmen (identity): We have an internal endpoint to force a resync for an org: `POST /internal/admin/resync-authz` with body `{"org_id":"acme-inc"}`. I'll run it for acme-inc now; it will rebuild token_alias cache and rehydrate rolebindings. NOTE: internal-only, will create audit events.

deploy-bot: [system] authz-resync job 98765 completed (duration 38s). Cleared 1 stale token alias mapping.

dmitri (eng): We also pushed a hotfix to token rotation handler to publish an alias update event to the cache invalidation stream (rolling restart to idp-proxy). Patch id: PR#4589. Rolling deploy started.

alice (support): Ben, after the resync can you retry the failing action? If still 403 we'll apply a safe workaround (temporarily grant your human user owner on the project) while we finish the deploy.

ben (acme-admin): Retried at 1725014230 — buttons are back and the curl returns 200. Thanks.

dmitri (eng): Deploy rolled out to 3/3 idp-proxy instances at 1725014800. Added extra logging and a defensive resync on rotation path. We'll monitor for recurrence.

alice (support): Glad it worked. Summary for the ticket: root cause = token alias mapping race after service-key rotation causing authz cache to hold stale principal -> role bindings; temporary mitigation = run internal authz-resync or log out/in and use personal key; permanent fix = publish alias-update event from rotation path (deployed). Will keep monitoring and reopen if it repeats.

ben (acme-admin): Confirming access remained stable for the next 30m. Thanks all, please keep me posted if you need any more logs. :thumbsup:

carmen (identity): Internal follow-up: adding extra metric for alias-update-latency and a small alert if alias rehydration exceeds 30s.

alice (support): Closing this Slack thread; will attach notes to SR-10234 and include remediation steps in the ticket. If anything flares, reopen and ping us. :white_check_mark:
